article_briefs.brief: Tata Motors raised its all‑cash offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share, valuing the deal at €3.91 billion and adding an €85 million credit facility with MUFG Bank to fund the increase.

Tata Motors’ €3.91‑billion bid for Iveco is now final at €14.40 a share; shareholder support, especially from Exor (27.06 % stake) and other large investors holding about 20 % of shares, will decide if the 80 % acceptance threshold is met.

Stellantis, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and its EV subsidiary signed a definitive agreement to expand their partnership into advanced vehicle technology and product development, with manufacturing in India at the FIAPL 50:50 joint venture for over 50 global markets.

Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Stellantis formalised an expanded collaboration that combines Tata’s vehicle architecture with Stellantis’ global product‑development expertise, targeting vehicle production in India for export to more than 50 markets.

Tata Motors lifted its offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share after activist Petrus Advisers rejected the prior price; three major investors controlling about 20.4 % of Iveco have yet to tender, keeping the deal at risk ahead of the 26 October deadline.

key_points.text: Tata Motors increased its cash offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share, raising the transaction value to €3.91 billion and financing the additional €85 million via a credit facility with MUFG Bank.
The €14.40 per share price is Tata Motors’ best and final offer, with no further increase planned.

Exor holds 27.06 % of Iveco’s shares (43 % of voting rights) and has pledged its stake, while Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital and Petrus Advisers together own about 20 % of Iveco, making their participation crucial for reaching the 80 % acceptance threshold.
If completed, the combined Tata‑Iveco entity would generate roughly €21 billion of annual revenue and sell about 5,90,000 vehicles each year.

Tata Motors and Stellantis expanded their partnership, signing a definitive agreement to co‑develop vehicles using Tata’s advanced product technology and vehicle architecture, with manufacturing to be done in India at the 50:50 FIAPL joint venture for more than 50 global markets.

industry_context.text: Analysts warn that a failed Iveco takeover would force the Italian commercial‑vehicle maker to fund Europe’s costly transition to cleaner commercial vehicles without the financial backing of a larger parent.

Stellantis operates a portfolio of 14 automotive brands across Europe, North America, South America, the Middle East, Africa and Asia‑Pacific, underscelling the global scale of the commercial‑vehicle market.

article_briefs.brief: Tata Motors needs to win over roughly 27% of Iveco’s silent shareholders to reach the 80% acceptance needed for full control of the Italian truck maker; about one‑third of non‑promoter votes opposed the deal despite a sweetened offer of €14.40 per share. The combined business would generate about €21 billion revenue and sell over 590,000 vehicles.

Analysts forecast Tata Motors’ commercial‑vehicle unit to post Q2FY27 revenue growth of around 44‑45% YoY and profit up to 44% YoY, driven by around 43% volume expansion, though margins may stay pressured amid input‑cost inflation.

Tata Motors displaced Mahindra to become India’s second‑largest passenger‑vehicle maker in April‑Sept FY27, posting a 43% rise in domestic dispatches to over 3.9 lakh units, aided by a 59% surge in utility‑vehicle sales.

Iveco shareholders approved all resolutions for Tata Motors’ €3.91 billion acquisition, lowering the mandatory acceptance threshold from 95% to 80% and clearing the way for a post‑offer demerger and delisting.

Iveco’s extraordinary general meeting endorsed Tata Motors’ takeover bid, confirming the €14.40 per‑share offer (up €0.30) and the cut in the acceptance threshold to 80%, with the tender period running until 26 Oct 2026.

key_points.text: Tata Motors must persuade silent shareholders holding about 27% of Iveco’s common shares to achieve the 80% acceptance needed for full control, after about one‑third of non‑promoter votes opposed resolutions.
The acquisition price was increased to €14.40 per share, valuing the deal at approximately €3.91 billion.
Shareholder approval reduced the minimum acceptance threshold from 95% to 80%, simplifying completion of the €3.91 billion takeover.
Post‑acquisition, the combined commercial‑vehicle business is projected to generate annual revenue of about €21 billion and sell over 590,000 vehicles.

Tata Motors’ CV unit is expected to record Q2FY27 revenue of Rs 24,218.4‑24,638.1 crore (up 43.6‑45.4% YoY) and profit growth of up to 44.3% YoY, supported by ~43% volume growth; margins remain under pressure.

Tata Motors overtook Mahindra to become the second‑largest passenger‑vehicle manufacturer in India for April‑Sept FY27, with dispatches up 43% to over 3.9 lakh units, driven by a 59% rise in utility‑vehicle sales.

industry_context.text: Domestic passenger‑vehicle dispatches in India grew 28.3% to around 26.4 lakh units in April‑Sept FY27, indicating robust sector growth.

article_briefs.brief: Tata Motors must win support from Iveco’s silent shareholders, who own about 27% of common shares, to reach the 80% threshold needed for full control. About 52.9% of Iveco’s shares backed the deal, while non‑promoter votes against key resolutions totalled roughly 13.7% for the chair appointment. The offer was sweetened to €14.40 per share. The combined business would generate around €21 billion revenue and sell over 590,000 vehicles.

Analysts preview Tata Motors CV Q2 FY27, expecting volume growth of about 43% YoY (≈42.7‑43% depending on the broker) and revenue up 44‑45% YoY to roughly Rs 24,218.4‑24,638.1 crore. Adjusted PAT forecasts diverge at 44.3% versus 25.7% growth. Margins are under pressure despite a 2.5% net price hike since July, with mixed outlooks on EBITDA margins.

Three investors hold about 20.4% of Iveco’s common shares and could earn roughly €63 million at the €14.40 offer, plus €288 million in extraordinary dividends. As of 21 October, about 33.4% of shares had been tendered; the offer closes on 26 October, and Tata needs 80% acceptance. Iveco’s defence business was sold to Leonardo for €1.7 billion.

A market roundup lists Tata Motors among companies whose September‑quarter earnings, credit rating updates, fundraising plans, regulatory developments and new business wins will be tracked on 23 October.
Tata Motors reported Q2 FY27 consolidated profit of ₹1,257 crore, with revenue rising 36.3%. Shares fell about 4% ahead of the results, trading around ₹397.80.

key_points.text: Tata Motors must secure 80% shareholder acceptance to fully acquire Iveco; currently about 52.9% of shares have backed the deal, while silent shareholders hold roughly 27% of common shares.
The offer price for Iveco was increased to €14.40 per share from €14.10.
The combined Tata‑Iveco business would generate annual revenue of about €21 billion and sell over 590,000 vehicles.
As of 21 October, about 33.4% of Iveco shares had been tendered; the offer closes on 26 October, and Tata needs to reach the 80% threshold.
Three investors holding about 20.4% of Iveco’s common shares could gain roughly €63 million at the €14.40 offer price, in addition to €288 million extraordinary dividends received in April.
Tata Motors CV’s Q2 FY27 volume grew around 43% YoY, with LCV volumes up 53.1% YoY and MHCV volumes up 31%.
Revenue for Tata Motors CV is forecast to rise 44‑45% YoY to roughly Rs 24,218.4‑24,638.1 crore.
Adjusted PAT forecasts diverge, with estimates of 44.3% growth (JM Financial) and 25.7% growth (Motilal Oswal).
Margins are expected to stay under pressure despite a 2.5% net price hike since July, with differing views on EBITDA margin trajectory.
Tata Motors posted Q2 FY27 consolidated profit of ₹1,257 crore and revenue up 36.3%; its shares fell about 4% ahead of the results, trading near ₹397.80.

industry_context.text: The commercial vehicle sector faces geopolitical headwinds, but Tata Motors CV delivered ~43% YoY volume growth, outperforming peers.
Iveco’s defence business was sold to Leonardo for €1.7 billion, reflecting activity in the defence‑vehicle segment of the broader commercial vehicle market.
